channel.title: Vinofilo
channel.description: Vinofilo: stories, places and craft of Italian wine. Grapes, regions, winemaking and serving, told with a point of view.

item.title: San Martino, the day every must becomes wine
item.description: 11 November, Saint Martin’s Day: the origins of the feast, St Martin’s summer, Italy’s regional new-wine traditions and what to open on the day.

item.title: What wine goes with pumpkin? Autumn’s trickiest pairing
item.description: Risotto, tortelli mantovani, velvety soup or roast pumpkin: which wine to choose when the sweetness of pumpkin and squash throws the glass off balance.

item.title: Smoke, fat and tannin: the best wine for a barbecue
item.description: Ribs, bistecca alla fiorentina, lamb, chicken, vegetables and fish from the grill: which Italian wine to choose, why it works and at what temperature to serve it.

item.title: Franciacorta vs Trento DOC: Italy's Two Sparkling Capitals Compared
item.description: Lake against mountain: how Franciacorta and Trento DOC differ in history, climate, rules, Satèn and Riserva, and what it means in the glass.

item.title: Buying wine online in the UK and US: a guide to the big shops
item.description: Majestic, The Wine Society, Naked Wines, Berry Bros., Wine.com, Total Wine and Wine Access: how to read them if you live in Italy and what they are really for.

item.title: What wine to drink with carbonara, amatriciana and cacio e pepe
item.description: Guanciale, pecorino and pepper lay down the law. Which wine to choose with Rome’s three great pasta dishes, from Cesanese to Frascati, and why it works.

item.title: Lugana, the Lake Garda white that won over the world
item.description: Turbiana, clay soils and a denomination straddling Lombardy and Veneto: why Lugana travels so well abroad, and how to read its styles.

item.title: What wine goes with risotto? What goes in the pan decides the glass
item.description: Milanese, al Barolo, all’Amarone, seafood or radicchio: how to choose the wine for risotto, starting with the one you pour into the pan.

item.title: Soave, the white that grew tired of playing second fiddle
item.description: From supermarket staple to Garganega on volcanic and limestone soils: why Soave deserves a second look, from the Classico hills to Recioto.

item.title: Buying wine online in France and Germany: the biggest shops
item.description: Vinatis, Millésima, Twil, iDealwine, Hawesko, Vinello, Belvini: who they are, what shipping costs and what to know about excise duty when buying from abroad.

item.title: Italia Nostra’s Red List: the beauty we risk losing
item.description: The Red List of endangered cultural heritage is now online. Why it matters to wine lovers too, since wine comes from the very landscape that needs protecting.

item.title: Merlot Day, 7 November: rehabilitating the grape Sideways mocked
item.description: International Merlot Day falls on 7 November: from Pomerol to Ticino by way of Friuli and Bolgheri, the grape’s story and what to open on the day.

item.title: Marsala, the great Italian wine we locked in the kitchen
item.description: From John Woodhouse to Florio, from egg Marsala to its revival: the history, categories and redemption of Italy’s most underrated fortified wine.

item.title: Decanter Fine Wine Encounter: London opens a thousand wines in two days
item.description: On 6 and 7 November the Decanter Fine Wine Encounter returns to The Landmark in London: what a fine wine is and how to survive a big tasting.

item.title: FIVI wine market 2026: a thousand growers, a trolley and Bologna
item.description: From 21 to 23 November BolognaFiere hosts the 15th Mercato dei Vini FIVI: a thousand independent growers selling with no middlemen. How to get around.

item.title: Buying wine online in Italy: apps, marketplaces and fast delivery
item.description: Vivino, Amazon, Winelivery, Svinando, Esselunga and Wine-Searcher compared on shipping, delivery times and user feedback, and who each one really suits.

item.title: Montepulciano: the Abruzzo grape or the Tuscan town?
item.description: Montepulciano d’Abruzzo and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano share only a name: grapes, regions, rules and how to tell them apart on the label.

item.title: Cinque Terre wine, the vineyard that climbs in steps
item.description: Dry-stone walls, monorails, Bosco, Albarola and Vermentino. The wines of the Cinque Terre and Sciacchetrà, a passito that survives only while the terraces are farmed.

item.title: Merano WineFestival 2026: five days of wine at the Kurhaus
item.description: From 6 to 10 November the 35th Merano WineFestival returns to the Kurhaus: its history, the WineHunter selections, what to expect and what to open.

item.title: Benvenuto Brunello 2026: Montalcino opens its doors to the 2022
item.description: From 19 to 23 November Montalcino presents Brunello 2022 and its other new releases: what to expect from the 35th edition and what to open at home.

item.title: Where to buy wine online in Italy: the big online wine shops compared
item.description: Tannico, Vino.com, Callmewine, Xtrawine, Bernabei and Signorvino compared: size, shipping and what users say, to help you choose where to buy wine online.

item.title: The best red wines under 15 euro, a map by appellation

item.title: Valtellina, the Nebbiolo that climbs the dry-stone walls
item.description: Terraces, dry-stone walls and Chiavennasca, or how mountain Nebbiolo is made in Valtellina, from the five subzones to Sforzato from dried grapes.

item.title: International Sherry Week 2026: seven days to stop snubbing Jerez
item.description: International Sherry Week returns from 2 to 8 November: what Sherry is, how to read its styles and what to pair with it, Italian dishes included.

item.title: Wines for aperitivo: sparkling, rosé and the art of not overdoing it
item.description: Sparkling wines, crisp whites, rosés, vermouth and spritz: which wines to choose for an Italian-style aperitivo and how to pair them with fried bites, olives and salumi.

item.title: Cantine Aperte a San Martino 2026: tasting the new wine straight from the vat
item.description: From 1 to 15 November the wineries of the Movimento Turismo del Vino open their doors for the new wine. How to plan, what to ask, what to expect.

item.title: What wine goes with sushi: bubbles, Riesling and the reds to leave at home
item.description: Soy, wasabi, salmon and tempura: why dry sparkling wine, Riesling and rosé work with sushi, and which wines to avoid. With Italian examples.

item.title: Hospices de Beaune 2026: the auction that sets the price of Burgundy
item.description: On 15 November, at the Halles de Beaune, the 166th Vente des Vins des Hospices: its history, how the auction works and why the whole market is watching.

item.title: Prosecco explained: DOC, DOCG, Cartizze and Rive
item.description: DOC, DOCG, Asolo, Cartizze, Rive and Col Fondo: a map of Prosecco, from the village near Trieste to the Glera grape and the UNESCO-listed hills.

item.title: Vino novello 2026: Italy’s new wine is uncorked on 30 October, by law
item.description: Italian vino novello 2026 arrives on 30 October: the rules, carbonic maceration, how long it keeps, how it differs from Beaujolais Nouveau and why it lost its shine.

item.title: How many bottles of wine for a dinner party? The sum nobody wants to do
item.description: How many glasses in a bottle, how much wine per person, what order to serve it in and at what temperature: a practical guide for a dinner or a party.

item.title: Carignan Day 2026: on 29 October we toast a rehabilitated grape
item.description: 29 October is International Carignan Day: from the Languedoc to Priorat, from Chile’s Maule to the Sulcis, what to know about Carignano and what to open.

item.title: Hong Kong Wine & Dine 2026: the harbour where wine pays no duty
item.description: From 29 October to 1 November Hong Kong opens its Wine & Dine Festival on the harbour: history, Bordeaux, what to expect and what to open at home.

item.title: Barolo and Barbaresco: same grape, two characters, a few kilometres apart
item.description: Communes, soils, minimum ageing and named vineyards: what really separates Barolo and Barbaresco, two Nebbiolo wines with the town of Alba between them.

item.title: Dolcetto isn’t sweet, and it may be Langa’s most honest red

item.title: Wine with mushrooms and truffles: what to pour when the forest comes to the table

item.title: Barbera, the people’s grape that decided to grow up

item.title: Chestnuts and wine: novello, and everything that comes after

item.title: Noble rot, the fungus that turns grapes to gold

item.title: What wine goes with pizza: a practical guide, topping by topping
item.description: Margherita, cured meats, quattro formaggi, pizza bianca and vegetables: which wines work with pizza, and why bubbles and cool reds almost always win.

item.title: Harvest day, who decides it and how they know

item.title: Champagne Day 2026: on Friday 23 October we open northern France

item.title: Barolo en Primeur 2026: buying a wine that does not yet exist

item.title: Italian wine exports in 2026: what the first-half figures really say

item.title: Milano Wine Week 2026: nine days to drink the city (not the trade fair)

item.title: New York Wine Experience 2026: Italian wine faces the tariff test

item.title: Italy’s 2026 harvest, region by region: the earliest vintage and the figures nobody would give

item.title: Hostaria 2026: tasting Verona on foot, from piazza Bra to piazza dei Signori

item.title: Alba white truffle fair 2026: what to drink on the festival weekends
item.description: From 10 October to 6 December Alba hosts the 96th White Truffle Fair: its history, the programme and the Langhe wines to open on those weekends.

item.title: Italian wine guides 2027: the winners so far, and where the critics agree
item.description: Bibenda, Winemag, DoctorWine and Gambero Rosso: the first 2027 guide winners, the wines that recur across rankings and the calendar of upcoming releases.

item.title: Nebbiolo, Italy’s most difficult (and greatest) grape
item.description: Pale colour, fierce tannin, late ripening: why Nebbiolo tests both those who grow it and those who drink it, from Barolo to Valtellina.

item.title: Etna, the volcano that redrew the map of Italian wine
item.description: Nerello Mascalese, Carricante, ungrafted bush vines and 142 contrade: why Etna is Italy’s most talked-about wine region, and what lies beyond the myth.

item.title: Metodo Classico or Charmat: what really changes in the glass
item.description: Second fermentation in bottle or in tank, months on the lees, bubbles and aromas: Franciacorta, Trento DOC and Prosecco, without the snobbery.

item.title: Wine serving temperature: why we get reds and whites wrong
item.description: Reds too warm, whites ice-cold: why “room temperature” is a misunderstanding, and the right serving temperatures for every style of wine.

item.title: Orange wines: the white that behaves like a red (and divides the table)
item.description: What orange wines are, why they are not the same as natural wine, from Georgian amphorae to Oslavia, and how to pair them with food without fear.

item.title: The right wine glass: how much does glass shape really matter?

item.title: Amarone, the wine born of waiting: appassimento, Recioto and Ripasso
item.description: How drying grapes in Valpolicella’s fruttai creates Amarone, what links it to Recioto and Ripasso, and why its style is up for debate today.

item.title: How to read an Italian wine label without being seduced by it

item.title: To decant or not: when a decanter helps and when it does harm
item.description: Removing sediment or adding oxygen? When to decant a young wine, when to protect a fragile old red, and what to do with whites and sparkling wines.

item.title: A wine cellar at home: what you really need to age wine
item.description: Stable temperature, humidity, darkness and calm: what matters when storing wine at home, in a wine fridge or a cupboard, and which bottles are worth the wait.
